what: The G5c native-speaker review of every whole-word محمد in the Grades 6-12 page-truth corpus. This file IS the clearance brief §4c requires; it is not a heuristic and nothing else in this repo may decide which محمد is which.
reviewer_role: native-speaker reviewer of record for gate G5c, named on the Grades 6-12 curriculum workbook Change Log as row H-0001

polarity.prophet: the Prophet — the salutation is required and the gate keeps demanding it
polarity.person: an ordinary named person — no salutation, and the gate must stop demanding one

polarity_note: the reviewer's marks were correct and the document's legend was wrong; Amena confirmed 2026-09-17 and the legend was corrected to match
source_file: 08_Grades 6-12 LP Build/_g5c_native_speaker_review_2026-09-17/Q2-decisions.json in the hyasin270/rumi-agent-home workspace repo — GITIGNORED there and absent from this repo, which is why the decided list is carried here as data rather than read from disk
derived_how: All 298 decided rows are carried, none dropped. Three descriptive columns from the source — occurrences, books and a quoted example sentence — are NOT carried: they are not read by the gate, and the examples are pages of textbook prose that do not belong in a public repo. The ' †' marker on 9 rows is a marker in the review DOCUMENT meaning 'this row quotes an editor's note rather than the printed book'; it is not part of any name and is stripped here.
matching: Keyed on the WORD SEQUENCE, not the byte string: each name is split on whitespace, each word has its Arabic combining marks (U+0610-U+061A honorific signs, U+064B-U+065F and U+0670 aeraab, U+06D6-U+06ED Quranic marks) removed and its edge punctuation trimmed, and a flagged محمد is cleared only when the surrounding words match a `person` entry with the same محمد in the same slot. The LONGEST matching entry rules; on equal length a `prophet` entry wins. No match means the gate fails, always.
